initialJsGzipBytes.reason: Decision: retain the 512000 B total entry-plus-scene gzip ceiling while replacing Phaser. The Three.js WebGL2 spike measured 201792 B gzip including fixture inputs (renderer ADR); product bytes are measured by tools/scene-budget.mjs, not inferred from the spike.

assetBytes.reason: Decision: every reviewed atlas image and animation manifest served from worlds/fixture/assets/reviewed. 256 KiB is about nine times the first reviewed set (28 kB), room for the rest of the wave's art.

textureBytes.reason: Decision: retain 16 MiB for everything the renderer allocates apart from the world's atlas pages (atlasTextureBytes). Account unique Texture identities across effects, reflections, generated RGBA8 labels and content textures, conservative full-resolution RGBA16F + depth/stencil renderer output, tier-scaled PassNode RGBA16F + depth/stencil (320x200 low; 640x400 medium/high), BloomNode RGBA16F bright target and two five-level chains with floored dimensions. Source: three@0.187.0 Renderer._getFrameBufferTarget, PassNode and BloomNode.setSize. This bounds allocated storage, not driver residency. WebGPURenderer storage is keyed by Texture identity, not shared image Source (common/Textures.js and each backend texture utility).

atlasTextureBytes.reason: Decision: 32 MiB of decoded RGBA8 atlas pages, two full 2048x2048 pages (the largest page the asset build packs). The renderer uploads one Texture per page the reviewed index lists and per selected material page, and counts each once; material renditions are chosen within what remains. About twice the issue 137 multi-page journey world (four pages, 17040000 B), which tests/ci/dev-world.journey.browser.test.mjs measures on both backends.

firstSceneRenderMs.reason: The Web Vitals 'good' Largest Contentful Paint threshold (2.5 s), measured from renderer construction to the first drawn committed scene.

frameTimeMs.reason: Decision: retain the p95 unsmoothed requestAnimationFrame interval ceiling at the 30 fps laptop floor (Wave 4 section 9.3). This cadence check is distinct from GPU-complete pan latency: the #67 RTX 2060 SUPER high-tier Three.js WebGL2 spike measured p50/p95 1.8/2.0 ms at 960x540 DPR1; product timing is a post-merge maintainer step.

entityCount.reason: Decision: the most drawn entities one scene supports, about seventeen times the golden scene's fifteen.

patchApplicationMs.reason: Decision: the slowest committed snapshot or patch draw, half of a 60 frames per second frame so a commit never drops a frame on its own.

reconnectMs.reason: Decision: the first reconnect delay (SCENE_RECONNECT.firstDelayMs, 1 s, apps/web/src/projection.ts) plus 2 s for the join and snapshot, from the client observing its scene socket drop to the next ready scene.

referenceMeasurements.scope: Renderer bake-off spike; not measurements of the product adapter. Product GPU-complete pan timing remains the maintainer step after merge.

wsl2ChromiumAngleGlOverD3D12.caveat: Suspect-clock flag from failed peer candidates; maintainer reports real clock and working Three.js WebGL2.

productCorrectnessMeasurements.source: timeout 3600 taskset -c 0-3 pnpm run qualify:wave4; evidence/visual/captures.json (both SwiftShader backends, 36 tier comparisons)
productCorrectnessMeasurements.scope: Software correctness and accounted allocation: four-core qualification plus one-core WebGPU stress. Low uses Lambert and a half-resolution scene pass into the unchanged canvas. GPU-complete latency remains the post-merge maintainer measurement; reference measurements above are from the bake-off spike.
productCorrectnessMeasurements.runtimeBudgetSource: qualify:wave4 evidence/test-e2e.log; four-core CPU affinity, both SwiftShader backends; unsmoothed rAF cadence, not GPU-complete latency
productCorrectnessMeasurements.oneCoreWebgpuSource: Historical command and renderer source: https://github.com/clockgrove/clockgrove/blob/190ff17/apps/web/scene-budgets.json; benchmark provenance remains at that immutable commit.
